Requirement: Given the user is not logged in, When the user selects Create Account, Then the account registration page must be displayed with the following mandatory fields: Username Email address Password Confirm password Age Avatar selection And each field must be visually identified as required with a *
Notes: Registration displays Username, Email, Password, Confirm Password, Age and Avatar. Team confirmed Age is optional, so the missing * on Age/Avatar is accepted. Required text fields are marked with *.

Acceptance Criterion: AC1.1.2: Prevent submission when mandatory fields are empty
Requirement: Given the user is on the registration page, When one or more mandatory fields are empty, Then the system must not submit the registration request and display an error message with each invalid field visually highlighted. For example: Username → “Please enter a username.” Email address → “Please enter an email address.” Password → “Please create a password.” Confirm Password → “Please confirm your password.”

Given the child enters a username shorter than 3 characters or longer than 20 characters, When the child attempts registration, Then the system must reject the username and display “Username must be between 3 and 20 characters.” and the child must not be able to proceed until a valid username is entered.

Given the child enters a username that belongs to an existing account, When the system checks username availability, Then the system must prevent registration with that username and display “That username is already taken. Try another one.” and account creation must not proceed using the duplicate username.

Acceptance Criterion: AC1.1.5: Remove leading and trailing spaces (Username spaces)
Requirement: Given the child enters spaces before or after their username, When the field is validated, Then all leading and trailing spaces must be removed before username length and uniqueness checks are performed.
Given the entered email does not follow a valid email format, When the field is validated, Then the system must reject the email and display “Please enter a valid email address.”

Given the child is entering their password, When characters are entered, Then the password must be masked by default and a Show/Hide Password control must allow the entered password to be temporarily displayed.
Notes: Masking and Show/Hide were directly exercised; the retained canonical screenshot primarily shows registration validation.

Requirement: Given the user has entered a password and confirmation password, When the two values do not match, Then the system must prevent account creation and display “Passwords do not match.”.

Given all required information is valid, When the user submits the registration form, Then the system must create one account, display a success state and direct the user into the appropriate RimbaQuest experience.
Notes: Valid Web registration created one account and entered the authenticated experience.

Requirement: Given an account creation request is being processed, When the user presses the submission button multiple times, Then the system must process only one registration request and must not create more than one account.
Notes: Repeated Create Account presses produced only one account.

Requirement: Given the submitted information is valid, When account creation fails because of a server or network error, Then the system must inform the user that registration was unsuccessful and must not create a partial or duplicate account.
Notes: Forced registration network/server failure was distinguished and did not create a partial account.

Requirement: Given the user has an existing RimbaQuest account, When valid credentials (username/email & password) associated with that account are submitted, Then the system must authenticate the user and display their RimbaQuest account.

Given the user enters invalid login credentials (username/email & password) that do not match a valid RimbaQuest account, When the user attempts to log in, Then access must be denied and a clear error message must be displayed.
Given one or more mandatory login fields are empty, When the user selects Log In, Then the system must prevent submission and each empty mandatory field must be visually identified.
Notes: Empty login fields were blocked and visually identified without submission.

Requirement: Given the user has previously saved discoveries, cards or progress, When the user successfully logs in, Then the system must retrieve the saved information associated with that account.

Acceptance Criterion: AC1.2.5: Handle Login Network or Server Failure
Requirement: Given the user has entered valid login details, When login cannot be completed because of a network or server failure, Then the system must display a connectivity/system error rather than incorrectly reporting invalid credentials.
Notes: Login connectivity/server failure was reported as a system error rather than invalid credentials.

Requirement: Given the child is logged in, When they select Log Out, Then the authenticated session must end and the user must return to the unauthenticated experience.
Given the user is on the login page, When the user selects Forgot Password, Then the system must display the password-recovery page with an email-address field and a Send Recovery Link action.
Notes: Forgot Password opened the recovery page with email field and Send Recovery Link.

Requirement: Given the user is on the Forgot Password page and the entered email is empty/does not contains a valid email format/not linked to any RimbaQuest account, When the user selects Send Recovery Link, Then the system must not submit the recovery request and an inline error message must appear below the field. For example: Empty field → “Please enter an email.” Invalid format → “Please enter a valid email address.”
Notes: Empty, malformed and unlinked recovery emails showed inline errors and did not submit.

Requirement: Given the child is logged in, When they select their profile, Then the profile page must display the profile information such as username, level, avatar, and collection progress.
Given the child is viewing their profile, When they select Edit Profile, Then the system must display the profile information that the child is permitted to edit, including username and avatar.
Notes: Edit Profile opened with permitted username and avatar controls.

Requirement: Given the child enters a new username that satisfies the approved username validation rules (must not contain fewer than 3 characters or more than 20 characters or is already assigned to another account), When they save the profile, Then the new username must replace the previous username, display on subsequent Profile and relevant account screens, and is recognised during subsequent login attempts.

Given approved avatar options are available, When the child selects a different avatar and saves the profile, Then the selected avatar must become the child's active profile avatar and must be displayed consistently on subsequent Profile and other relevant account screens.

Given the child has edited their username and avatar without saving, When they attempt to leave the Edit Profile screen, Then the system must display a warning that the unsaved changes will be lost and provide the child with an option to remain on the page or discard the changes.
Notes: Leaving Edit Profile with unsaved username/avatar changes offered remain or discard.

Requirement: Given the child is logged in, When the child selects Discover Locations from the main navigation, Then the system must open the Discover Locations page and display the available wildlife/nature locations Notes: Focus on KL/Klang Valley for iteration 1.

Acceptance Criterion: AC2.1.2: Do not guarantee wildlife sightings
Requirement: Given wildlife information is displayed for a location, When the child views the location card or location details, Then the system must not state or imply that a particular species is guaranteed to be present and must use wording such as: “Previously observed here” “Wildlife you may encounter” “Species recorded around this area” And avoid wording such as: “You will see...” “Guaranteed wildlife...”

Given location information is being retrieved, When the Discover Locations page is loading, Then the system must display a loading indicator or placeholder and must not incorrectly display “No locations found” before loading is complete.
Notes: Delayed locations GET showed a spinner and Loading wildlife locations...; No locations found was not shown before the list appeared.

Requirement: Given the child is viewing Discover Locations, When the page loads, Then a search field must be displayed above the location list and it must clearly indicate that the child can search by location name or area with a placeholder “Search locations or areas”

Given the location list contains a location matching the entered keyword, When the child enters part or all of the location name, Then the system must display matching locations and hide non-matching results.
Given one or more locations belong to an area matching the search term, When the child searches using that area name, Then the system must display the matching locations.

Given a matching location exists, When the child enters the keyword using different capitalisation, Then the same relevant results must be returned. Example: kl, KL and Kl should return the same matching locations.

Given a location name contains the entered keyword, When the child enters a partial location name, Then the system must return that location. Example: Location: Kuala Lumpur Bird Park Search: “Bird” Then the location should appear.
Given no location matches the entered keyword, When the search is performed, Then the system must display “No matching locations found.” and must not treat the result as a system error.

Story Title: Capture or Upload a Wildlife Photo
Requirement: Given the child is logged into RimbaQuest, When the child selects Record a Discovery from the home screen, Then the system must open the wildlife camera interface.

Story Title: Capture or Upload a Wildlife Photo
Requirement: Given the wildlife camera interface is open, When the camera is ready, Then the system must display: the live camera preview; the photo capture button; access to the device photo gallery; an option to exit/return from the camera; basic guidance indicating that the child should point at the wildlife and capture a photo.

Story Title: Capture or Upload a Wildlife Photo
Requirement: Given the child is viewing the live camera preview, When the child presses the photo capture button, Then the system must capture exactly one image and display the captured image for review.
Notes: Take photo captured exactly one image and opened Review Your Photo. The live webcam frame was not retained in evidence.

Story Title: Capture or Upload a Wildlife Photo
Requirement: Given the child is on the wildlife camera interface, When the child selects the gallery option, Then the system must allow the child to select one image from the device and display the selected image for review.

Story Title: Capture or Upload a Wildlife Photo
Requirement: Given a photo has been successfully captured or selected, When the image is loaded, Then the system must display the wildlife photo clearly and allow the child to enlarge the image where the photo preview supports it.
Notes: Selected/captured photo displayed clearly and Enlarge photo opened a closable enlarged view.

Story Title: Capture or Upload a Wildlife Photo
Acceptance Criterion: AC3.1.6: Review and Continue With Selected Photo
Requirement: Given the child has successfully captured or selected a valid wildlife image, When the image has been successfully accepted by the system, Then the system must automatically proceed to the Choose a Wildlife Category screen and must retain the selected wildlife photo as part of the current discovery.

Story Title: Capture or Upload a Wildlife Photo
Acceptance Criterion: AC3.1.7: Do not proceed without a photo
Requirement: Given no valid wildlife photo has been captured or selected, When the child remains on the camera screen, Then the system must not open the wildlife-category selection screen.
Notes: Normal Web flow enforced a photo, but the deployed API accepted confirmed no-photo discoveries that affected progress and were omitted from Web Gallery.

Story Title: Capture or Upload a Wildlife Photo
Requirement: Given the child has captured or selected a wildlife photo, When the child chooses to retake or replace the photo before completing the discovery, Then the system must allow another photo to be captured or selected and the new photo must replace the previous photo for the current discovery.
Notes: Retake returned to the camera and a new capture replaced the previous in-progress photo.

Story Title: Capture or Upload a Wildlife Photo
Acceptance Criterion: AC3.1.9: Retain Photo During Temporary Connectivity Loss
Requirement: Given the child has captured or selected a valid image, When the system cannot process or upload the image due to a network or server error, Then the system must display “Your photo couldn't be uploaded. Please try again.” and provide a Try Again option.
Notes: Failed photo POST at confirm displayed Your photo couldn't be uploaded. Please try again. Photo, species, category and location were retained; Confirm & Save remained available to retry. A webcam frame was observed during retest and was not filed as evidence.

Requirement: Given the wildlife photo has been successfully captured or selected, When the photo is accepted, Then the system must automatically display the Choose a Wildlife Category screen.

Given the category-selection screen has loaded, When supported categories are available, Then the system must display the currently supported wildlife categories (Mammals, Birds, Butterflies, Reptiles)

Given a wildlife category is available, When it is displayed, Then the category option must show: category name; representative image. This makes it easier for a 9–12-year-old child to recognise the correct category.

Given the child is viewing the available wildlife categories, When the child selects one category, Then the system must store that category as the current discovery category and automatically open the corresponding species-selection screen.

Acceptance Criterion: AC3.2.5: Display species based on selected category
Requirement: Given the child selects a wildlife category, When the species-selection screen opens, Then the system must display only supported species belonging to the selected category. Example: Selected category: Mammals → Common Marmoset, Malayan Tapir, Long-tailed Macaque, Silvered Langur, etc.

Given the child has entered a species-selection screen, When the child uses the Back control to return to category selection, Then the system must retain the uploaded wildlife photo and allow a different category to be selected.
Notes: Back from species selection retained the uploaded photo and allowed a different category.

Requirement: Given a supported species is shown, When the child views that species option, Then it must display: species common name; species reference image; wildlife category.

Given the child is on the species-selection screen, When the child enters text into the search field, Then the system must filter the displayed species to those whose common name contains the entered text.

Given a supported species contains the entered search text, When the child enters only part of the species name, Then the matching species must still be displayed. Example: Search: marmo → Common Marmoset

Given a supported species matches a search term, When the search term is entered using different capitalisation, Then the same matching species must be returned. For example: marmoset, Marmoset, and MARMOSET should return the same relevant result.

Given the entered search text does not match any supported species within the selected category, When the species list is filtered, Then the system must display “No matching species found.” and must not display unrelated species as matches.
Given the species list has been filtered, When the child clears the search field, Then all supported species within the selected wildlife category must be displayed again.
Given multiple species are displayed, When the child selects one species, Then the system must store exactly one species as the selected species for the discovery.

Given the child is viewing the Confirm Discovery screen, When the child taps the wildlife photo, Then the system must display an enlarged version of the image and returning from the enlarged view must not change the selected species or discovery information.
Notes: Enlarging the confirm photo and returning left species and discovery details unchanged.

Requirement: Given the child reaches the Confirm Discovery screen, When the discovery location is being provided, Then the system must allow the child to choose between: Automatic Location — use the device's current location at the time the discovery is submitted; or Manual Location — allow the child to manually select or provide the location associated with the wildlife discovery.

Given the child chooses Use My Current Location and the application has the required location permission, When the system prepares the discovery information, Then the system must retrieve the device's current location at the time the discovery is submitted and use it as the discovery location.
Notes: Use my current location with granted geolocation supplied a current discovery location.

Requirement: Given the child chooses to provide the location manually, When the manual-location option is selected, Then the system must allow the child to select or enter an appropriate location associated with the wildlife discovery.

Acceptance Criterion: AC3.3.5: Location Permission Denied or Unavailable
Requirement: Given the child selects Use My Current Location, When location permission is denied or the device location cannot be determined, Then the system must: inform the child that the current location cannot be accessed; not prevent the discovery process from continuing; and provide the option to enter or select the location manually.
Notes: Denied/unavailable geolocation explained the fallback and still allowed manual location entry.

Requirement: Given the Confirm Discovery screen has loaded successfully, When the child reviews the discovery, Then the system must display: wildlife photo; species common name; wildlife category; and discovery location.

Given the child is on the Confirm Discovery screen, When the child selects Choose Another Species, Then the system must return to the species-selection screen and retain: wildlife photo; previously selected wildlife category; While allowing the child to select another species.
Notes: Back from Confirm Discovery returned to species selection and retained the wildlife photo and Mammal category. Team accepted Back as the Choose Another Species path.

Acceptance Criterion: AC3.3.8: Do not save before confirmation
Requirement: Given the Confirm Discovery screen is displayed, When the child has not selected Yes, Record My Discovery!, Then the system must not create a confirmed discovery record and must not update the child's collection.
Notes: Collection/progress did not change while Confirm Discovery was displayed and before Confirm & Save.

Requirement: Given the discovery has been successfully saved, When the save operation completes, Then the system must automatically open the Success screen.

Given the child selects Yes, Record My Discovery!, When the system fails to save the discovery, Then the system must display “Your discovery wasn't saved. Please try again.” while retaining: wildlife photo; selected category; selected species; recorded location; And provide a Try Again option.
Notes: A 500 discovery save retained photo, Mammal, Asian Elephant and KL Forest Eco Park, but showed Unable to save rather than Your discovery wasn't saved. Please try again. Retry remained Confirm & Save.

Requirement: Given the child has previously recorded the same supported species, When another valid discovery of that species is confirmed, Then the system must save the new observation as a separate discovery record.

Acceptance Criterion: AC4.1.1: Unlock card after first confirmed discovery
Requirement: Given the child has successfully recorded a supported species that is currently Undiscovered in their collection, When the discovery is confirmed and saved through Epic 3, Then the corresponding Wildlife Card must change from Undiscovered to Discovered in that child’s personal collection.

Acceptance Criterion: AC4.1.2: Do not unlock before successful save
Requirement: Given the child has selected a supported species during the discovery flow, When the discovery has not yet been successfully saved, Then the corresponding Wildlife Card must remain Undiscovered and the child’s collection progress must remain unchanged.
Notes: The Wildlife Card remained Undiscovered and progress was unchanged before a successful save.

Requirement: Given the child has already unlocked a Wildlife Card for a species, When the child records another confirmed discovery of the same species Then the system must retain one Wildlife Card for that species and must not create a duplicate card.

Acceptance Criterion: AC4.1.4: Do not increase unique-species count for repeat discovery
Requirement: Given the child has already unlocked the Wildlife Card for a species, When another confirmed discovery of the same species is saved, Then the child’s unique-species collection count must not increase and the overall collection completion percentage must remain unchanged.

Given a Wildlife Card is in the Discovered state, When the child opens the card, Then the system must display: common name; scientific name; wildlife category; discovery status; protection status, where verified data is available; habitat; diet; ecological role; species description.
Given a Wildlife Card is in the Discovered state, When the child opens the card, Then the system must display the card’s: species-specific HP; species-specific base power/default attack.

Acceptance Criterion: AC4.1.7: Display future ability slots as locked
Requirement: Given the Wildlife Card has been unlocked in Iteration 1 and the child has not yet unlocked quiz-based abilities, When the card is displayed, Then the system may display up to three specialised ability slots as Locked and the locked abilities must not be available for use in battle. This prepares the card for the later progression: Quiz 1 → Ability 1 Quiz 2 → Ability 2 Quiz 3 → Ability 3

Given the child has not recorded a confirmed discovery of a supported species, When that species appears in My Collection, Then the system must display it in an Undiscovered visual state that is clearly distinguishable from a Discovered card.

Acceptance Criterion: AC4.1.9: Provide limited information for undiscovered species
Requirement: Given a species is in the Undiscovered state, When the child opens that species entry, Then the system must display only the approved pre-discovery information, including: common name; scientific name; wildlife category; short species introduction; broad habitat information; discovery hint; reference image.
Notes: An undiscovered species page showed only approved pre-discovery information.

Requirement: Given a species is in the Undiscovered state, When the child opens its species page, Then the system must not provide access to discovered-only content, including: unlocked Wildlife Card; personal discovery gallery; battle availability; quiz progression; unlocked specialised abilities.
Notes: Undiscovered species page did not expose gallery, battle, quiz or unlocked-ability controls.

Requirement: Given the child has previously recorded one or more confirmed discoveries of an unlocked species, When the child opens the Gallery tab for that species, Then the system must display the wildlife photos associated with that child’s confirmed discovery records for that species.

Acceptance Criterion: AC4.1.12: Display multiple observations in gallery
Requirement: Given the child has recorded the same species more than once, When the Gallery tab is opened, Then each successfully saved observation for that species must be displayed as a separate gallery entry.
Notes: API retained repeat no-photo observations, but Web Gallery displayed only the later photo-backed UI observation.

Acceptance Criterion: AC4.1.13: Display discovery details in gallery
Requirement: Given a saved wildlife observation appears in the Gallery, When the child opens that observation, Then the system must display the corresponding: wildlife photo; recorded location.
Notes: The visible photo-backed entry showed its location; no-photo API observations were omitted rather than represented consistently.

Requirement: Given the child is logged into RimbaQuest, When the child selects My Collection, Then the system must open the personal Wildlife Card collection page.

Given the child opens My Collection, When the collection page loads successfully, Then the system must display one collection entry for every supported species available in the current RimbaQuest species catalogue.

Given the collection page is displayed, When each species entry loads, Then the system must display the species as either: Discovered, or Undiscovered based on the child’s confirmed discovery records.

Given the child opens My Collection, When the collection page loads, Then the system must display: number of unique supported species discovered; total number of supported species; collection completion percentage. Example: 4 / 20 Wildlife Discovered — 20% Complete

Acceptance Criterion: AC4.2.5: Calculate progress using unique species only
Requirement: Given the child has recorded one species multiple times, When overall collection progress is calculated, Then that species must count only once toward the unique-species discovery total.

Acceptance Criterion: AC4.2.6: Browse collection by wildlife category
Requirement: Given the child is viewing My Collection, When the child selects a wildlife category such as: Mammals; Birds; Butterflies; Reptiles, Then the system must display only species assigned to the selected category.
Notes: Mammals, Birds, Butterflies and Reptiles chips showed only species from the selected category.

Requirement: Given a category filter is active, When the child selects All, Then the system must display all supported species regardless of wildlife category.
Notes: All restored the same complete collection shown before category filtering.

Acceptance Criterion: AC4.2.8: Update progress after new species discovery
Requirement: Given the child successfully records a supported species that was previously Undiscovered, When the collection data is updated, Then: that species must change to Discovered; the unique-species discovery count must increase by exactly one; the collection completion percentage must be recalculated.
Notes: First saved previously undiscovered species changed that card to Discovered and increased unique count by one.

Requirement: Given the child opens My Progress or the relevant progress view, When the progress information loads, Then the system must display the number of discovered species and total supported species for each wildlife category. Example: Mammals: 3 / 8 Birds: 5 / 10 Butterflies: 1 / 6 Reptiles: 2 / 5
Notes: UI category totals sum to 151 while the deployed catalogue/progress total is 152.

Story Title: View and Interact With the Wildlife Card Battle Interface
Requirement: Given the child is logged into RimbaQuest, When the child selects Card Battle, Then the system must open the battle card-selection interface.

Story Title: View and Interact With the Wildlife Card Battle Interface
Acceptance Criterion: AC8.1.2: Display Wildlife Cards for Battle
Requirement: Given the child has discovered Wildlife Cards, When the battle card-selection screen is displayed, Then the frontend must display available Wildlife Cards that may be selected for battle.

Story Title: View and Interact With the Wildlife Card Battle Interface
Requirement: Given a Wildlife Card is shown on the battle-selection interface, When the child views the card, Then the interface must display: species common name; species image; HP; and base power/default attack.

Story Title: View and Interact With the Wildlife Card Battle Interface
Requirement: Given one or more Wildlife Cards are displayed, When the child selects a card, Then the interface must clearly indicate which card has been selected.

Story Title: View and Interact With the Wildlife Card Battle Interface
Requirement: Given the child has selected a Wildlife Card, When another card is selected before continuing, Then the new card must visually replace the previous selection.
Notes: Selecting a second available battle card visually replaced the first as the sole selection.

Story Title: View and Interact With the Wildlife Card Battle Interface
Requirement: Given the child proceeds from card selection, When the battle screen is opened, Then the frontend must be capable of displaying: the child's selected Wildlife Card; opponent Wildlife Card; species names; species images; HP display or HP bars; base power/default attack information; and Basic Attack control.

Story Title: View and Interact With the Wildlife Card Battle Interface
Requirement: Given the battle frontend prototype demonstrates the end of a battle flow, When the corresponding outcome state is displayed, Then the interface must provide a: Victory state; and Defeat state.
Notes: Victory was displayed in the Web prototype. Defeat exists as a UI state but is unreachable: opponent HP 110 / attack 20 and every catalogue card win before player HP reaches 0.
